Command: Do not forget what Amalek did
Summary: Deuteronomy 25:19 closes the Amalek law with a ban on forgetting: 'thou shalt not forget it.' Remembrance is commanded twice over — once as a duty, once as a refusal to let it slip.
Commandment: Do not forget what Amalek did to you.
Application: Scripture's stated context: Amalek met Israel by the way and smote the hindmost of thee (Deuteronomy 25:18). Debated: whether this remembrance today is a historical duty, a warning against cruelty to the weak, or both, is genuinely disputed — this row does not settle it.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: Amalek met Israel by the way and smote the hindmost, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God (Deuteronomy 25:18).
Function: This governed neighbours, not priests — it belongs to the ordering of Israel's common life. Deuteronomy 25:19 closes the Amalek law with a ban on forgetting: 'thou shalt not forget it.' Scripture gives the context: Amalek met Israel by the way and smote the hindmost, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary. The restraint is the prohibition itself: do not forget what Amalek did to you.
